frame.title: Haryana's 30-day challenge: 100 Gurugram roads by 7 November 2026
frame.what: On 8 October 2026 Rajesh Khullar, Chief Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister, directed GMDA, MCG and HSVP to identify 100 roads of at least 500 m each in poor condition and upgrade them by 7 November 2026 (recarpeting, end-to-end paving, streetlights, lane marking, footpaths, signage, encroachment removal), with a QR-coded board on each road naming the department, the officer and the dates, and a signed weekly scorecard in the newspapers every Saturday. Ten of the roads are to be 'iconic'.
frame.status: As of 23 October 2026 only GMDA's share is public: 27 stretches (20 master roads, 7 iconic roads) reported by the Hindustan Times on 12 October. The MCG and HSVP shares, the QR boards and the weekly scorecards could not be found in any public source.
sources: Directions of Rajesh Khullar, Chief Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister, meeting with GMDA, MCG and HSVP at the PWD Rest House, Gurugram, 8 Oct 2026 (DIPRO Gurugram press note; reported by HT, ToI, Tribune, Jagran, Bhaskar on 8 and 9 Oct 2026)

Hindustan Times, 12 Oct 2026, 'GMDA identifies 27 roads for repair under 30-day challenge' (Abhishek Behl; quoting Amit Godara, Executive Engineer, GMDA), https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/gurugram-news/gmda-identifies-27-roads-for-repair-under-30-day-challenge-101791746544459.html

GMDA tenders page (gmda.gov.in/tenders.html), read 23 Oct 2026: special-repair tenders for several listed roads, e.g. 'Special repair of master road dividing sector 32/39' (2026_HRY_555082_1, DNIT 17 Oct 2026)
frame.geometry: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Nominatim, Overpass and the OSRM demo router, looked up once at build time on 23 Oct 2026 by tools/roads_geocode.py; lines are approximate (about 10 m) and the ends of several stretches were not stated by the source. Each road carries a 'geo' field saying how its line was made.
